expected.why: Criticises the financial system's restrictions on how Bitcoin is used; no named party.

sentences.text: The amount of freedom Bitcoin offers us is something we voluntarily limit in response to the impositions placed on us and restrictions placed on us by the financial system itself.

before.text: It just has to change our behavior and the way we interact with it.
When I use platforms that take Bitcoin, I can't spend certain coins with them, even though the network itself doesn't care about the origin of my coins.
They are all fungible by the protocol.
When you get down into tiny amounts, you have dust limits and stuff like that.
We don't need to go into that kind of hair -splitting pedantry here.
The point is, why am I not sending coins that were coin -joined and choosing instead to send coins that were withdrawn from some squeaky clean?
Why am I making a distinction between the two when the protocol doesn't care about the difference?
Because the merchant does, or the third -party payment provider they're using, does.
And as long as our behavior gets modified, it doesn't matter if the protocol remains neutral or not, because our behavior is already limited.
